org: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Kenya (reported by The Standard)
quote: online job scammers trick Kenyans to apply for jobs, only for them to be taken to Myanmar where they are forced to commit cybercrimes.

org: Prime Cabinet Secretary and Cabinet Secretary for Foreign and Diaspora Affairs, Musalia Mudavadi (reported by The Eastleigh Voice)
quote: Fraudulent recruitment has increasingly shifted online, with job scams circulating through Facebook, Telegram, WhatsApp, TikTok and job websites.

org: NAPTIP Director-General Binta Adamu-Bello (reported by Peoples Gazette)
quote: Ms Adamu-Bello urged Nigerians to verify overseas job offers, avoid unofficial recruitment channels, and promptly report suspicious activities to relevant authorities.

org: Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development, State Minister Balaam Barugahara (reported by Daily Monitor)
quote: Many young people are losing money to traffickers and fraudulent companies. Please stay alert. Always verify that the recruiter is licensed before engaging with them.

org: Minister for Foreign Affairs Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, with the Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations (reported by GBC)
quote: If you are being recruited, please check if the recruiting agency is known to government.

org: Government of Ghana (Ablakwa, Ghana Immigration Service, EOCO; reported by GBC)
quote: Many trafficking cases originate from unlicensed recruitment agencies and fake job advertisements circulated on social media.

org: Africa Defense Forum, summarising the Associated Press investigation of 10 October 2024
quote: A slick online marketing campaign called 'Alabuga Start' shared hundreds of recruiting videos targeting African women with the promise of a good-paying job and a free flight to Russia.
